results.fact: Trapper Lake camp elevation (~5,000 ft in itinerary/climate vs 4,170 ft waypoint)
results.correct_value: Trapper Lake is at about 4,170 ft
results.evidence: The lake's reference elevation is 4,170 ft, and the USGS elevation service returns 4,169 ft at two points on the lake surface (48.43996,-121.00369 and 48.4405,-121.0015). This agrees with waypoints[1], beta and the approach variant; only the two text copies saying ~5,000 ft are changed. The day gain/loss figures built on a higher camp are NOT recomputed (a computed figure is not allowed) and are flagged separately below.

results.fact: Itinerary day gain/loss built on a ~5,000 ft camp (day 1 loss 700 ft, day 2 gain 2,700 ft) vs a 4,170 ft lake and 7,530 ft summit
results.evidence: With the lake at ~4,170 ft, the summit day from the lake to the 7,530 ft summit must gain more than the stated 2,700 ft, and day 1 must lose more than 700 ft after crossing the high ground above Pelton Basin. No source states per-day or car-to-car gain for this approach; a trip report gives only times (5.5 h in, 6 h out). Re-deriving the days would be a computed figure, so nothing is patched.

results.fact: dist_km (Approach one way) holds the round-trip figure
results.evidence: Trip reports on the Cascade Pass - Pelton Basin - Trapper Lake approach give times (5.5 h in, 6 h out with heavy packs) and describe a faint fisherman's path, but none states a one-way mileage. dist_km 30.58 km (19 mi) is the itinerary round trip, but a one-way value cannot be sourced or halved.

results.fact: Whether the route tops out on Trapper Mountain's summit
results.evidence: A new search found only the same ski-descent reports (2012 first descent; spring ascents) and a note that the couloir was climbed in the 1970s by a Roper party; none states whether parties continue from the top of the couloir to the 7,530 ft summit. Not settled.

A 2007 report gives 6,115 ft of car-to-car GAIN and a trail listing surfaced by search gives 6,085 ft over 7.3 mi (both including the ~800 ft drop to Upper Garfield Lake), consistent with gain_ft 6,100. No source states a loss figure, and setting loss_ft equal to gain on an out-and-back is the refused loss_ft class, so loss_ft 800 is left flagged.

results.fact: September: 'outside the best season' vs best_season/season Jul-Sep
results.evidence: New sources cut both ways: a report notes the route gets harder every year late in the season, with the direct line to Lucky Pass melted to ice and parties forced into a roundabout traverse (supporting 'marginal' for September); the other ascents found are June-August. No source states a season window that includes or excludes September.
No new cumulative gain figure found; the 2003 traverse report gives no stats and the SummitPost trip report returned 403. The only figures remain 8,300 ft (one report) and the net 6,862 ft.

A further search surfaced only the same accounts: one party's 30 m rope was not long enough for the crux pitch in one rappel (intermediate anchor needed), another found 30 m worked to reach a ledge. A new candidate page (lemkeclimbs) is gone (404). Accounts still disagree.

results.fact: Season this route is actually climbed in
results.evidence: The season column currently holds a sentence, which another session owns and must not be edited here. Sources still present Tye Peak mainly as a winter snowshoe/ski extension of Skyline Ridge; no summer window is documented by two sources.

Figures still disagree: the Mountaineers route page gives 4 mi round trip / 1,100 ft for Skyline Ridge and Tye Peak (less than the 1,415 ft net rise, so likely ridge-only), WTA says the Tye extension more than doubles the 1,100-1,300 ft to the ridge, other listings give 1,500 and 3,300 ft. No two sources agree on 1,800 or 2,400.
